subject: Request: temporary uptime waiver + proposed monthly remedy allocation for pilot
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Eve Torres <eve.torres@starlab.ai>, Mohammed Khan <m.khan@starlab.ai>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 18:02:00 -0800
Subject: Request: temporary uptime waiver + proposed monthly remedy allocation for pilot

Eve / Mohammed —

Thanks again for the productive call earlier. Starlab's pilot looks promising and we want to keep timelines tight. The one sticking point from your side was the baseline uptime/credits language in our standard SLA. To move the pilot forward without reopening the entire contract, we can offer a targeted operational exception for the 3-month pilot window plus a clear monthly remedy allocation formula. Proposal below: 

- Baseline uptime: Redwood standard 99.95% (no change)
- Pilot exception: allow up to 8 hours/month of scheduled batch maintenance or known degradation related to large data imports (must be notified 72h in advance) without triggering full remedy calculations
- Remedy calculation (for unplanned availability loss beyond exception): monthly service credit = min( (monthly_fee * downtime_minutes / total_minutes_in_month), credit_cap )
- Proposed credit_cap during pilot: 20% of monthly fee
- Latency: maintain p95 < 800ms for API calls under pilot's expected traffic; incidents that are strictly latency-related will use a separate, limited credit pool (proposal attached)

Attachments: Redwood_SLA_Template_v2.pdf (highlighted where we suggest the carveout), SOW-pilot-attachment.xlsx (traffic profile).

Ask: can you confirm Starlab is comfortable with the 8h/month graceband and the 20% cap for the pilot? If yes, we can circulate a short amendment (1 page) and sign via DocuSign. If you want a different cap or a tiered cap tied to usage, flag the desired numbers and we’ll run them by finance.

Happy to hop on a 30-minute call tomorrow to finalize.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

Redwood Inference — production-first LLM inference
From: Eve Torres <eve.torres@starlab.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mohammed Khan <m.khan@starlab.ai>, Connor Lewis <connor@starlab.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:17:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Request: temporary uptime waiver + proposed monthly remedy allocation for pilot

Thanks Karthik — appreciate the quick follow-up and the pragmatic approach. A couple of clarifications from our side after reviewing the draft redlines (attached as Starlab_Redlines_20261114.docx):

1) Graceband: 8 hours/month feels high for our use case. Can we consider a 4-hour allowance for standard maintenance and a separate 4-hour allowance that would cover one-off large imports (we'd need to provide a pre-notice for that second bucket)?

2) Credit cap: 20% is reasonable, but we'd prefer a tiered cap for the pilot so small customers (like our internal pilot tenant) aren't overcompensated relative to usage. Proposed pilot cap: 15% for customers < $5k MRR, 20% for $5k–$50k, 25% for > $50k. We'll supply anonymized usage bands for the pilot population if you accept that approach.

3) Latency: we can accept a separate limited credit pool for latency, but we also want a short SLA metric that ties failures to a clearly defined p95 window and the monitoring source (Synthetics from our region).

We attached redlines and a short Excel with our suggested tiering. If you (and finance) can sign off on tiered caps and a dual-bucket graceband (4h standard + 4h large-import with notice), we can proceed to sign the short amendment. Otherwise we need to escalate to procurement for a final sign-off.

Proposing a 30-minute sync today at 14:00 PT if that works — Connor will be on the call for SRE alignment.

Best,
Eve Torres
Head of Integrations, Starlab AI
Eve.Torres@starlab.ai
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Eve Torres <eve.torres@starlab.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: temporary uptime waiver + proposed monthly remedy allocation for pilot

Eve — thanks for the clear counter. Internal notes below (looping Ben for finance confirmation):

- Dual-bucket graceband (4h standard + 4h large-import w/ notice): acceptable for a 3-month pilot only. We need the notice window for the large-import bucket to be 72 hours and a max of one large-import carveout per month. Please confirm you'll adhere to the notice window in the amendment language.

- Tiered cap: we can accommodate a tiered pilot cap but need predictable upper bounds for Redwood's risk modeling. Accepting your proposed tiers but will ask finance to reserve flexibility: "pilot cap adjustable by usage bands but absolute cap cannot exceed 25% for any single customer during the pilot." Ben — can you confirm whether finance is comfortable holding 25% as absolute maximum for this deal?

- Remedy formula language: please accept the simplified text below (we'll add it as an amendment paragraph):
  • Remedy calculation for availability: monthly service credit = (downtime_minutes / total_minutes_in_month) * monthly_recurring_fee, subject to the pilot cap above.
  • Latency: credit pool separate, triggered only when p95 measured by Starlab Synthetics exceeds 1000ms for > 30 continuous minutes across >= 3 distinct reachability checks.

Next steps: if Starlab confirms the dual-bucket and the tiered cap with the absolute 25% ceiling, we'll prepare a one-page amendment and route for signature. If Connor or your SRE team needs different monitoring text, we can add a short appendix (SRE monitoring sources permitted: Starlab Synthetics, Redwood edge metrics).

Tagging Ben for the finance check and an explicit "ok to route DocuSign" from legal if this sounds good.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
VP, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Eve Torres <eve.torres@starlab.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 16:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: temporary uptime waiver + proposed monthly remedy allocation for pilot

Perfect — thanks Eve and Laura. Quick recap and ask: 

- Starlab confirms dual-bucket: 4h standard + 4h large-import (72h notice; max one large-import carveout per month) — Eve to confirm in reply.
- Tiered pilot cap accepted with Redwood absolute maximum 25% per customer during pilot — Eve to confirm band boundaries acceptance in writing.
- Remedy formula: use the simplified text Laura provided; latency triggers as written, monitoring sources allowed as listed.

Assuming Starlab confirms the two bullets above, I'll have Legal and Contracts prepare a one-page amendment (will reference Redwood_SLA_Template_v2.pdf and include the Starlab_Redlines_20261114.docx as an exhibit). We will route for DocuSign and aim for signature within 48 hours so the pilot can start next week.

Proposed calendar: 30-min call today at 14:00 PT if you can still make it — otherwise we’ll do an abbreviated call tomorrow morning. DocuSign link and amendment draft will be shared once we have your written confirmation on the two points.

Thanks team —
Karthik
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
